mcqs.question: Which statement best describes Mendel's experimental approach in his pea‑plant studies?

options.A: He selected true‑breeding (homozygous) pea plants, performed controlled cross‑pollination, and analyzed the traits in the F1 and F2 generations.
options.B: He mixed seeds from different varieties in a bag and observed the resulting plants without controlling pollination.
options.C: He used only wild‑type peas and recorded their natural variations over several seasons.
options.D: He relied solely on observations of plant height in a single generation.

mcqs.answer: He selected true‑breeding (homozygous) pea plants, performed controlled cross‑pollination, and analyzed the traits in the F1 and F2 generations.
mcqs.explanation: Mendel began with pure‑breeding (homozygous) pea varieties, manually transferred pollen to control which plants mated, and then recorded the characteristics of the first (F1) and second (F2) filial generations. This systematic method allowed him to discover consistent ratios. Options B, C and D describe uncontrolled or incomplete observations, which Mendel did not use.

mcqs.question: In Mendelian genetics, a dominant trait is best defined as:

options.A: A characteristic that appears in the phenotype when at least one dominant allele is present.
options.B: A characteristic that appears only when two recessive alleles are present.
options.C: A trait that never appears in any generation.
options.D: A characteristic that is always masked by other traits.

mcqs.answer: A characteristic that appears in the phenotype when at least one dominant allele is present.
mcqs.explanation: A dominant allele masks the effect of a recessive allele, so the associated trait is expressed if the genotype contains one or two copies of the dominant allele (heterozygous or homozygous dominant). Options B, C and D describe recessive or incorrect concepts.

mcqs.question: A recessive trait, according to Mendel's findings, is defined as:

options.A: A characteristic that is expressed only when two recessive alleles are present.
options.B: A characteristic that appears even if one dominant allele is present.
options.C: A trait that is always expressed regardless of genotype.
options.D: A characteristic that dominates over all other traits.

mcqs.answer: A characteristic that is expressed only when two recessive alleles are present.
mcqs.explanation: Recessive alleles do not affect the phenotype when a dominant allele is present; they are expressed only in the homozygous recessive condition (rr). Options B, C and D contradict the definition of recessive.

mcqs.question: Mendel crossed true‑breeding tall (T) pea plants with true‑breeding dwarf (t) plants. In the F2 generation, what phenotypic ratio did he observe?
mcqs.explanation: The F1 generation from TT × tt is all heterozygous (Tt) and tall. When F1 plants self‑pollinate, the F2 generation shows a 3:1 phenotypic ratio (tall : dwarf) because three of the four possible genotypes (TT, Tt, Tt) produce the tall phenotype, while only tt gives dwarf. The other options do not match Mendel's observed ratio.

mcqs.question: If a true‑breeding yellow‑seeded (YY) pea plant is crossed with a true‑breeding green‑seeded (yy) plant, what will be the genotype of all F1 offspring?

options.D: Yy and yy in equal proportion

mcqs.explanation: Crossing homozygous dominant (YY) with homozygous recessive (yy) yields offspring that inherit one allele from each parent, resulting in the heterozygous genotype Yy for every F1 plant. Options A and C represent the parental genotypes, and D suggests a mixture that does not occur in this cross.

mcqs.question: In a monohybrid cross between a heterozygous yellow‑seeded plant (Yy) and a green‑seeded plant (yy), what are the expected phenotypic and genotypic ratios among the offspring?

options.A: Phenotypic 3 yellow : 1 green; Genotypic 1 YY : 2 Yy : 1 yy
options.B: Phenotypic 1 yellow : 1 green; Genotypic 1 Yy : 1 yy
options.C: Phenotypic 1 green : 3 yellow; Genotypic 1 yy : 2 Yy : 1 YY
options.D: Phenotypic 2 yellow : 1 green; Genotypic 2 Yy : 1 yy

mcqs.answer: Phenotypic 1 yellow : 1 green; Genotypic 1 Yy : 1 yy
mcqs.explanation: The cross Yy × yy produces two possible genotypes in equal proportion: Yy (yellow) and yy (green). Hence the phenotypic ratio is 1 yellow : 1 green, and the genotypic ratio is also 1 Yy : 1 yy. Options A, C, and D describe ratios for different crosses (e.g., Yy × Yy) and are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Mendel's experiments is a common misconception?

options.A: Mendel used true‑breeding pea varieties to ensure that the parental traits were uniform.
options.B: Mendel counted the number of offspring showing each trait to deduce ratios.
options.C: Mendel performed his experiments over many generations in a single season.
options.D: Mendel deliberately cross‑pollinated plants to control which gametes combined.

mcqs.answer: Mendel performed his experiments over many generations in a single season.
mcqs.explanation: Mendel's work spanned several years; he could not complete many generations within a single growing season. Options A, B, and D accurately describe his methodology, while C misrepresents the time frame of his experiments.

mcqs.question: If a pea plant displays the round seed shape, which of the following statements correctly explains why this trait is considered dominant?

options.A: The round shape appears only when the plant has two copies of the round allele.
options.B: The round shape can appear even if the plant carries one round allele and one wrinkled allele.
options.C: The round shape never appears if a wrinkled allele is present.
options.D: The round shape is expressed only when the plant is homozygous recessive.

mcqs.answer: The round shape can appear even if the plant carries one round allele and one wrinkled allele.
mcqs.explanation: A dominant allele masks the effect of a recessive allele, so a heterozygous genotype (Rr) still shows the dominant (round) phenotype. Option A describes a recessive requirement, C is false because the dominant trait can still appear with a recessive allele present, and D incorrectly labels the recessive condition as dominant.
